messages:
Alice M: Thinking out loud — can we introduce an "alert-floor" or "flooring" concept in the console so tiny SLO blips don't generate noisy notifications?
Ben K: +1 on the idea. We get a lot of <5% transient burns that create pages. A floor would reduce churn.
Carla R: curious how this differs from sampling/quiet windows. Flooring would just prevent notify unless severity >= floor, right?
Alice M: yeah — keep the SLO evaluation unchanged but gate notify. So teams still see the incident in UI, but it won't fan out to oncall until it crosses the floor threshold.
Ben K: That could help with pager fatigue. Need to be careful with edgecases (gradual ramps vs spikes).
DevOps Bot: deploy-runner: staged/notify-gate v0.3 started — tests for notify gating.
Dave L: API contract question: should flooring be a per-tenant field or per-SLO? I think per-SLO + inherit from tenant default.
Emily S: per-SLO with optional "inherit": true seems best. UI should surface the effective floor and allow preview in the rollout wizard.
Frank P: what about routing interplay? If floor prevents notify on the primary channel, do we still log to telemetry and to the fallback routing tier?
Alice M: yes, telemetry still records events; fallback routing (eg. audit-only channels) should get entries. Only paging/notifying channels are suppressed.
Carla R: implementation sketch: add `notify_floor` to notify policy proto (float 0-1). In evaluation path, before fanout we check effectiveSeverity >= notify_floor.
Carla R: code: ```json
{"notify_policy": {"notify_floor": 0.05, "channels": ["#pager","#alerts"], "fallback": "#audit"}}
```
Ben K: nice. Need migration: existing alerts should default to notify_floor = 0.0 (no suppression). Console should warn when enabled.
Emily S: UX: show a small tooltip "Minimum SLO burn to alert" and preview sample history with suppressed/not-suppressed markers. Also let owners simulate for last 7/30 days.
Dave L: quota concern: if suppressed alerts still generate storage/telemetry costs we might need a flag to `drop_telemetry_if_suppressed` for low-tier customers. But I'd rather keep telemetry for visibility.
Frank P: Agree keep telemetry. Could add an indexable flag `suppressed=true` so downstream pipelines can filter cheaply.
Alice M: rollout plan: opt-in flag on tenant, feature-flagged per-SLO in API; 2-week canary, then org-wide. Add a telemetry metric: `alert.notify_suppressed_count` and `alert.notify_suppressed_ratio` per-tenant.
Carla R: tests: unit evaluate path, integration fanout test, and an end-to-end UI preview test. Also add spec for time-series UX so suppressed windows are annotated.
Ben K: One more: coalescing with priority — if a bunch of small suppressed burns coalesce into a bigger window, guarantee a single notify at threshold crossing (no duplicate backfills).
Alice M: yes — fanout should dedupe by fingerprint and only emit notify on crossing event. Add an event state machine: suppressed->queued->notified.
Emily S: mockups incoming. I'll put a PR for the console tooltip and preview endpoint.
DevOps Bot: deploy-runner: staged/notify-gate v0.3 completed, canary flagged for tenant: rgx:dev-*
Dave L: logging note: include `floor_applied: true/false` in fanout logs so oncall can audit why an alert didn't page.
Frank P: sounds good. I'll add the proto change and a migration doc.
Alice M: thanks all. Next: let's discuss default value and recommended best practices in the docs — propose default 0.03 for service-type X, 0.0 for critical infra.
Ben K: +1. Meeting tomorrow 10am to finalize defaults and rollout checklist.
Alice M: cc @Carla R @Emily S for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
